words.meaning: done quickly and efficiently without unnecessary delay
words.example: The support team found an expeditious way to restore access without skipping the security checks.

words.meaning: quick to understand situations and notice what is important
words.example: Her perspicacious questions revealed a flaw in the proposal that everyone else had missed.

words.meaning: to estimate an unknown value between two known values
words.example: We can interpolate the missing June figure from the May and July data.

words.meaning: making a fault or offense seem less serious because of the surrounding circumstances
words.example: The manager considered the power outage an extenuating circumstance when reviewing the missed deadline.

words.meaning: impossible to stop or prevent from continuing
words.example: The inexorable rise in maintenance costs made replacing the old system the sensible choice.

phrases.meaning: to take the lead and coordinate an effort
phrases.example: Maya will run point on the launch and keep every team aligned.

phrases.meaning: to act early before a situation becomes harder to manage
phrases.example: We should notify customers now and get out ahead of it before rumors spread.

phrases.meaning: to try again after a mistake or unsuccessful attempt
phrases.example: That first demo was rough, so let's take a mulligan and restart from the login screen.

phrases.meaning: to strongly support or defend someone or something
phrases.example: My director went to bat for me when I proposed hiring another designer.

phrases.meaning: to discreetly ask around to learn about interest or opportunities
phrases.example: I'll put some feelers out and see whether anyone knows a reliable contractor.
